title: Kiln compatibility rules (<kiln>/compat-rules.json, <configDir>/compat-rules.json), format 1
description: Rules for closed-source DLL mods and other engines. A rule fires when every `when` matcher is present in this start (no matcher: it always fires). Actions: original-code (only a named Shroudtopia mod sees original bytes when its imported memcmp checks a recognised entry hook; no load-order change), defer (the native loader waits for the Shroudtopia host first pass when the target mod is enabled in the profile, bounded by max_wait_ms; absent or external hosts are not waited on), warn (tell the player), late (load the subject DLL after Kiln and ShroudForge: chain.ini [late]), disable (do not load the subject), before (dev.29: the subject DLL loads before the `target` DLL; the launcher keeps the subject early and loads the target late, whatever their late switches say, and moves nothing when that cannot be done). The launcher applies `late`, `disable` and `before` of chain entries when it writes chain.ini; kiln-core evaluates the same rules at boot end and at the first world, logs warnings, reports what is not applied yet, and switches off a mod the profile lists. Two files are read, the shipped defaults (<game>/kiln/compat-rules.json, may be empty) and then the player's (<configDir>/compat-rules.json, default <game>/kiln/config; the launcher's copy is <data>/profiles/<profile>/config/compat-rules.json): a rule of the second file with the same id replaces the first file's rule in place; other rules are appended. To switch a shipped rule off, replace it with a rule of the same id whose `when` cannot hold. A rule that does not validate (an unknown key included) is dropped with a warning and the others stay (so a reader from before dev.29 drops a `before` rule and keeps the others); a file that is not one JSON object with `format` 1 is ignored. Plain JSON: no comments. Matching and evaluation fixtures shared by the C++ core and the launcher's Rust reader: schema/fixtures/compat-rules/cases.json. Docs: docs/kiln/engines/README.md#closed-source-dll-mods.

rules.description: More than 512: the first 512 count, the readers (kiln-core, the launcher) log one line saying how many were ignored.

matcher.description: Exactly one key: module, engine, mod or symbol. Each value is 1 to 260 characters.

module.description: A DLL file name, case-insensitive; `*` matches any run of characters, `?` one character (`xhl-*.dll`). Matches the whole file name (give no path). A pattern with wildcards has at most 64 characters and 4 `*`. Present: a chain entry that is on (not switched off, not refused) or a module loaded in the process.

engine.description: An engine word as in crates/kiln-manage/src/engines.rs (`word`): emf, shroudforge, eml, set, enshwick, greeneye, shroudtopia, flame, shroudlink, ember, modloader-proxy, ultimate-asi-loader, aldrich-modmenu, livemap, shared-xp, reshade, chain-loader, and `kiln` (always present). Case ignored. Present: the profile lists an enabled mod of that engine, or one of its loaders is in the chain or the process. kiln-core knows an engine from the profile lists, ShroudForge's state and a few well-known DLL names; the launcher knows more (it classifies the chain DLLs).

mod.description: <engine>:<mod id>, e.g. `emf:coolmod`. Kiln's own native mods are `kiln:<id>` or `native:<id>` (the same mods); managed Kiln mods and plugins are `kiln:<id>`. The engine word ignores case, the id does not. Present: the active profile lists the mod and it is enabled.

symbol.description: A sigdb symbol name (`chat/ChatLogAdd`). Present: the hook map has an overlap on that symbol (hooks.json `overlaps`). kiln-core evaluates it from this session's overlaps, so only at boot end and at the first world; the launcher from the last session's hooks.json.

id.description: Unique in a file (the first of a repeated id stays). A rule of the player's file with a shipped rule's id replaces it.

when.description: Every matcher must be present for the rule to fire (at most 8). Empty or absent: the rule always fires.

subject.description: What the action is about: required for late, disable, before, defer and original-code, optional for warn. original-code: exactly one shroudtopia:<id> mod whose imported memcmp may see original entry bytes; no chain changes. defer: a native mod id, a declared DLL file name, or an exact package-relative companion path using forward slashes. Wait plans that include a native init use normal phases to keep init on its documented thread. late: a `module` (a chain entry; nothing else can load late). disable: a `module` (chain entries: the launcher leaves them out of chain.ini) or a `mod` (the core switches it off in the profile before the plugins read it; the launcher switches it off in the profile it writes) or an `engine` (the launcher leaves that engine's chain entries out; the core can only report it). before: the DLL that loads first, as a `module`, an `engine` (the launcher knows a chain DLL's engine by its exports and texts, whatever it is called) or a `mod` (a native mod of the profile, by its Library id); it stays early (in the proxy), also when its late switch is on. Subjects the core cannot apply show in hooks.json `rules` with `applied: false`.

target.description: before or defer only, required for both. defer: a shroudtopia:<id> mod enabled in the profile. before (dev.29): the DLL that loads after the subject. The launcher loads it late (chain.ini [late], marked `; kiln rule <id>`). Nothing moves, and the launcher shows a warning, when it cannot load late (EMF's loader, shroudlink's client addon), is not in Kiln's chain, matches the subject too, or another rule loads the subject late.

max_wait_ms.description: defer only, required: maximum wait after the Shroudtopia host starts its worker, including bootDelay.

message.description: Plain sentence for the player: what clashes and what Kiln does about it. Shown in the launcher and logged by the core; for before, also under both chain entries on the profile page and in the activation's notes.
